claim: Standard softmax cross-entropy rounds the target-logit gradient to exactly zero once the logit margin exceeds a precision cliff of about 5.5 (bf16), 16.6 (fp32) and 36.7 (fp64).

Under AdamW with weight decay, the post-memorization margin settles near log(1/eps): 18.4 at eps=1e-8, above the fp32 cliff; for eps>=1e-7 the equilibrium (<=16.1) sits below the cliff and standard CE settles without spiking.
contradictions: Prieto 2025 App. I and Thilak 2022: too large an eps can halt learning and grokking (syn-02)

syn-04 (Liu et al., wd=0 runs): eps=1e-6 only makes spikes rarer; eps=1e-5 removes them; Liu App. A.3.1 also argues weight decay keeps margins below ~16, which syn-01's measured equilibrium (18.4 at eps 1e-8) contradicts for wd=1

claim: With weight decay controlling the norm, slingshot spikes from the fp32 cliff slow and slightly degrade grokking (94.3+/-5.4% vs 100+/-0% on a+b mod 31, 1-layer Transformer, wd 1, eps 1e-8, fp32).
contradictions: ja-09: 15-seed replication finds no fp32 speed-up (8/15 vs 8/15 seeds ending >=95%); only spike removal and stability replicated

claim: Computing the loss in bf16 with standard CE badly hurts grokking; the margin-form fix restores it.

Training-loss spikes of more than 10^6x accompany grokking in the original openai/grok code at weight decay 0.01; the author calls them a fundamental part of grokking but also shows a case where they are not essential.
contradictions: syn-01: spikes are a numerical artefact that helps only when LayerNorm plus no/low wd makes them act as LR decay; syn-04: precision-driven spikes; ko-20 reads spikes as benign

claim: Spikes are best treated as a diagnosable numerical event: do not roll back or early-stop on them, but remove their cause (margin-form CE or eps>=1e-7) in the default arm and log margin to classify them.

Decoupled AdamW weight decay of about 1.0 on all parameters, including embeddings, is the switch that produces grokking in every non-English replication of the finite-set recipe; wd<=0.1 does not grok within 3e4-1e5 steps.
contradictions: ja-13 and zh-06 report grokking at wd 0 (50% split; Tian theory); syn-02 shows grokking without regularization is possible until softmax collapse

claim: Coupled L2 inside Adam at wd 1.0 collapses training (2.6% train accuracy for 40k steps).
contradictions: ko-20 mechanism claim about coupled decay is wrong

claim: Weight decay acts mainly on the embedding and decoder layers late in grokking (ExPLAIND, ICML 2026; wd 4.0, full batch, a>=b, mod 113).
contradictions: single-run case study

claim: Grokking delay scales to leading order as 1/(eta*lambda): theory and grids from Pracher et al. (MLP 84x90, transformer 42x45 grids), Luo et al. (Adam shell-core theory), Truong et al. (293 runs, R2 0.97 wd / 0.92 lr), Boursier et al. (gradient flow, order 1/lambda) and Xu et al. (ridge).
contradictions: Most theory assumes squared loss, coupled L2 or gradient flow (en-04); en-06 and en-07 share all four authors; strong decay prevents fitting (upper cutoff, en-04)

claim: At p=97, lr 1e-3, wd 1, full batch: grokking arrives near 1.3k-4k steps at a 0.5 split and near 2e4 steps at a 0.3 split.
contradictions: Kanda's 30-50% plateau at split 0.5 may be the commutation leak (inference)

claim: A random split of ordered pairs leaks commutative transposes into training; at train fraction f about f of off-diagonal held-out pairs have their transpose in train.
contradictions: arithmetic is the fr lane's and this report's own

claim: The official Grokfast EMA filter starts from the first gradient (not zeros), is applied once per optimizer step between backward() and step(), and its EMA preset is alpha 0.98, lambda 2.0; lambda 5 belongs to the MA variant.
Grokfast's algorithmic presets use weight decay 0.005-0.01 against a weakly regularized Adam baseline; no source tests Grokfast with AdamW wd 1.0.
Grokfast fails or is unstable in independent hands: exploding gradient norms (#9), unsolved fp16 GradScaler (#10), AdamW beating Grokfast+Adam (#12), and a 16-arm Zhihu A/B with 0/8 grokking arms.
contradictions: Zhihu A/B is single-seed, AI-assisted, cosine LR, batch 256, 10% split

claim: StableMax enables grokking without regularization but is not an accelerator over weight decay; perpendicular-gradient (OrthoGrad) groks faster than tuned weight decay.
contradictions: ja-03: StableMax wd0 ~60k epochs vs AdamW wd1 ~10k; syn-01: StableMax margins 3200-21252 and lower accuracy than fixed CE
en-24, en-26: spherical residual stream and per-row clipping grok fast without weight decay, but against weak (wd 0.01 or no-wd) baselines

claim: The l2 weight norm is not a reliable stand-alone progress measure.
contradictions: zh-13, ja-02, ja-25 see a norm peak or inflection at grok onset

claim: Epistemic uncertainty collapses sharply at grokking in in-context modular arithmetic (label-free diagnostic).
contradictions: report, not peer reviewed; in-context setting

claim: Early stopping and validation-loss checkpoint selection would end grokking runs during the plateau; validation loss can rise during the plateau.
Grokking step varies 2-3x across seeds and some seeds fail; at least 3 seeds are needed and single-seed negatives are uninterpretable.
Test accuracy can rise and fall several times before holding (non-monotone transition).
The ridge-regression paper (arXiv 2601.19791) was an ICML 2026 oral and an Outstanding Paper Honorable Mention, not simply a best-paper nominee.
contradictions: award tier rests on secondary pages; the ICML oral page shows no award label

claim: A larger learning rate (5e-3) can steer Adam to a memorizing rather than Fourier solution; lr 3e-4 slows or stalls grokking.
Freezing the weight norm or removing weight decay at memorisation stops grokking at p=97, eta 1e-3, lambda 1 (0/6 vs 3/3 baseline).
contradictions: small n; same author group as en-06; en-24/en-26 grok without decay via other norm constraints

claim: Presentation order of a fixed training set can dominate grokking: two fixed orderings reached 99.5% at epochs 487 and 659, IID reached 0.30% after 5,000 epochs (p=9973, 0.3% data); in shared-trunk multi-task training tasks grok in a consistent staggered order.
contradictions: single-author preprints; extreme low-data regime; norm/logit-scale papers explain delay under IID order (en-03, en-06)

claim: No independent multi-seed replication of Grokfast on transformer modular arithmetic against a tuned wd=1.0 baseline exists as of Oct 2026; the only new test (sparse parity, single seed) is out of regime.
contradictions: absence claim; searched by en-delta lane and five language lanes

claim: Train-only or label-free progress signals exist but are unvalidated on mod-p transformers: commutator defect (SCAN/Dyck), local learning coefficient, logit margin; representation metrics read at the grok step overstate converged values 3-5x.
contradictions: en-17 eigengap detector fails with ReLU

claim: No looped or weight-tied transformer study of modular-arithmetic grokking was found; the nearest is knowledge-graph QA where looping crosses an OOD grokking barrier.
contradictions: absence claim

claim: SGD fails at hyperparameters where AdamW reliably groks (modular arithmetic, sparse parity).
contradictions: same author group

claim: The grokking delay tracks the logit scale (R2 0.97), with the weight norm adding 1-2%; this links norm-based and precision-based accounts.
contradictions: single author
